pr_body:
This change simplifies and reduces the amount of boilerplate
code needed to get a device emulator up and running, thus reducing excise work
to writing tests.

Due to the change in EMUL_DEFINE and other code. This is a breaking-change for emulators.

Fixes #39486
pr_comments: @sjg20 would you mind taking a look?
Drafting to respond to comments not mentioned within this PR yet.
Converting to draft-mode to work on comments.

Made a large design change here:

After a bit more digging we only use a `struct {bus}_emul` to get at `struct emul` in emulator client-code so changing all of the function signatures to work directly with `struct emul` instead. If ever needed the {bus_emul} can still be accessed via `bus->emul`

Creators of emulators may never actually need to directly access {bus}_emul structs again, which is a good idea since they're more of a representation of an internal structure than a logical structure that should be reasoned with.
I will take a look at this by Friday

@yperess 

The includes must come after the forward-declaration otherwise we get their usages before the type's been declared when we include the other headers, leading to a *real* compilation failure.
This `#ifdef` should be above the case, or alternatively you should move the `#endif` up so that the `break;` is still there otherwise you'll fall through

This can be simplified as:
```
#define Z_EMUL_BUS(_dev_node_id)                                                \
	COND_CODE_1(DT_ON_BUS(_dev_node_id, i2c), (i2c),                                          \
		    (COND_CODE_1(DT_ON_BUS(_dev_node_id, espi), (espi),                           \
				 (COND_CODE_1(DT_ON_BUS(_dev_node_id, spi), (spi), (-EINVAL))))))
```

Not just used as:
`Z_EMUL_BUS(node_id, i2c, espi, spi)`
